RaceName: Lady Jane Bethell Memorial Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Won at Redcar and Thirsk for today's rider last season (both over 1m on good ground), but hasn't shown the same level of form in two runs this term; conditions suit and back on last winning mark.

RaceName: Lady Jane Bethell Memorial Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Two wins this term, latest at Nottingham last month (8.5f, good to firm); two close seconds since; an obvious contender but stamina to prove on first run at 1m2f (stays 1m1f).

RaceName: Lady Jane Bethell Memorial Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
OwnerName: Horn And Trumpet Lads & S & A Mares
Spotlight: Won twice last season, first time over this trip on good to firm at Yarmouth; hasn't done as well this term; now back on last winning mark.

RaceName: Lady Jane Bethell Memorial Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Last four wins have been over 7.5f/87.5f here, three on fast ground; beaten 0.5l by a stable companion over C&D on first try at 1m2f last time (Star Start 0.5l back in third); contender.

RaceName: Lady Jane Bethell Memorial Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Won over this trip for today's rider at Newbury last June (good to firm); rather inconsistent since, but fine second to an in-form rival at Chepstow last time (1m2f, good to soft; The Pug just behind in third); a possible off current good mark.

RaceName: Lady Jane Bethell Memorial Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Dead-heated in this race last season (1lb lower), and having run his best race since a wind op when a close third over C&D last time (Sunny Orange second) is one to consider.

RaceName: Lady Jane Bethell Memorial Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: 18-race maiden; some fair form this season, including when second at Chepstow two runs back; handles these conditions and has an each-way chance.

RaceName: Lady Jane Bethell Memorial Amateur Jockeys' Handicap
Spotlight: Ex-Micky Hammond; close third at Chepstow on stable debut in June (1m2f, good to soft; Alwazar was 0.5l in front in second); well beaten over 1m6f on AW last time; should fare better back down in trip.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: The first of two Listed wins last year came over C&D; out of form this season until respectable fifth of 14 in handicap at Sandown (1m) latest outing, when wearing first headgear (retained today); needs to build on that.

Used to represent same connections as Liberty Lane but performed near his best only a couple of times last season, including when a promoted fourth in this race (good); had gelding and wind operations before well beaten on reappearance in June in first-time headgear; sold for 35,000gns 19 days ago; one of his handicap wins was on good to soft and the other three were on soft, neither of which is likely today.

Lightly raced since winning twice on turf as a 3yo; while not at his best last season, he was still third to Liberty Lane in a 1m2f Listed race in November and isn't entirely dismissed reappearing in new headgear (replacing recent cheekpieces) for his first handicap since May 2024.

Acts on good to firm; effective with varied tactics and easily made all on his reappearance over C&D (good; 10lb higher today) in May; needs to bounce back from a poor show when never dangerous at just 7-1 for a top 1m2f handicap at York 17 days ago.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Close second in 1m2f Group 1 in 2024 was the peak of his career in Australia; lightly raced since and absent 420 days before his respectable seventh of 12 at 40-1 in Haydock handicap (7f) on British debut; well held at 80-1 in 1m Royal Hunt Cup at Ascot six weeks ago; dropped 5lb on the strength of those last two runs but this return to 1m2f needs to see a return to peak form.

Improvement in each of his three races this term; strong finishes when winning at Leopardstown (1m2f, yielding to soft) on second occasion and second of 11 there (1m1f, good; unraced on firmer) on latest, so it's not hard to believe that he remains capable of better; greatly respected.

Ended his time with Harry Charlton on a high for Pontefract win (1m2f, good to soft; has won on good to firm) last September; had three races in Bahrain in December-March, clearly best of those on first occasion and given wind surgery since latest; needs a career best.

Progressive 3yo for Andrew Balding in the first half of last year, culminating in a 1m2f handicap win at Royal Ascot (good to firm); sold for 775,000gns the following month but not seen again until well held in major 1m2f handicaps this summer at Epsom and York; hooded in the latter when getting hampered over 1f out contributed but he did not look like playing a major part at the time; player if surging back to his best.
Runner-up in 2024 on his only appearance at this track; reliable sort who hit new heights over 1m4f on last three outings, so this drop back in trip asks a question but he needs respect.

Took form to a new level on AW early this year, which he's not repeated but winning at Chester (1m2f, good) 18 days ago was a return to his best turf form; back up 3lb today, well held in this race two years ago (his only handicap here) and he also has more to prove on ground firmer than good.

Ended his time with Charlie Appleby on a low note (March 2024) and no revival in his four races at Meydan for another yard the following winter; 483 days off and switched stables again before well beaten at Epsom (1m2f, good to soft; 100-1) early last month, which has been followed by another 5lb fall but he's hard to latch on to at the moment.

Has won twice at this track, albeit in very different races to this; 1m2f wins at Newbury and Epsom (made all) on good ground in April and ran well again when third at Sandown this month on good to firm; each-way player if he's in the same form.

1-8 for William Haggas; second run for new connections when he resumed improvement to make all in ten-runner race at Leicester (1m2f, good; acts on good to firm) in June, well clear through the final 2f; those wins are two of the four times he's made the running, which will be more difficult in this larger field and after a 10lb rise but he looked good last time.

Beaten on his last 13 starts going back to May 2024 but he's run some big races and wasn't discredited in his two starts this term; third and tenth in the last two runnings of this race; claimer ridden for the first time as a handicapper and worth a second look despite wide draw.

Had sunk markedly in the weights before first-time blinkers saw him take a six-runner race at Newmarket (1m2f, good to firm) 11 days ago in clearcut fashion, coming from last for his first win since a 2yo; back up 5lb but maybe he's turned a corner in the headgear.

0-8 in handicaps but runner-up in three (two at 1m2f) and ran respectably when fourth at Newmarket on latest start; short of room when well held at this meeting last year; new cheekpieces join the tongue-tie.

Made an eye-catching reappearance from well off the pace in April and went mighty close when he reverted to front-running over that same Newbury 1m2f (good) in June; tongue tied first time in the latter and again on latest start when always prominent to prevail by a neck in something of a bunched finish at Windsor (1m2f, good to firm); a different 5lb claimer takes over today; back up 2lb but looks an each-way player.

RaceName: Thank You Kathy Burne Selling Handicap
Spotlight: Modest maiden for Edward Bethell but beat only two for new yard when ninth in 1m2f handicap at Pontefract last month; more is needed.

RaceName: Thank You Kathy Burne Selling Handicap
Spotlight: Winless since January 2024; raced mainly over hurdles subsequently and posted a solid fourth over hurdles at Uttoxeter 13 days ago; visor goes on for the first time.

RaceName: Thank You Kathy Burne Selling Handicap
Spotlight: Ended 2025 below par for Mike Murphy but she's returned in good nick for her new yard, placed in handicaps at Brighton (1m4f) and Lingfield (2m) this summer; very much one to consider dropped in grade.

RaceName: Thank You Kathy Burne Selling Handicap
Spotlight: Scored over hurdles but a modest Flat maiden for Brian Ellison; comes here in good nick over hurdles for new yard, sixth at Uttoxeter 13 days ago; not out of things back in this sphere.

RaceName: Thank You Kathy Burne Selling Handicap
Spotlight: Modest winning hurdler for Fergal O'Brien last autumn; came in last of six for new stable in 1m4f Catterick handicap 13 days ago; not easy to make a case for.

RaceName: Thank You Kathy Burne Selling Handicap
Spotlight: In good form without winning in handicaps, not enjoying a smooth passage when fifth of eight in 1m2f handicap at Redcar nine days ago; visor replaces cheekpieces; drops in grade now and holds leading claims.

RaceName: Thank You Kathy Burne Selling Handicap
Spotlight: Took a big step forward in first-time cheekpieces with third at Lingfield (11.5f) in May but she beat only one in 1m4f Epsom handicap 27 days ago; well in the mix if back on song here.

Looks rather quirky having jinked right in two of his races, unseating rider on first occasion; however, once straightening he knuckled down well in the Group 2 Superlative Stakes at Newmarket (7f, good to firm; got up in final stride) latest, taking record in completed starts to 3-3; now goes in headgear, which may prove beneficial; leading player, even with 3lb penalty.

Got loose beforehand but made all and won going away at Ascot (7f, good to firm) last time, taking record to 2-2; brings potential to this higher grade and represents the Cole yard that landed this prize a few times when Paul was at the helm; adds interest.

Made a promising debut behind stablemate Abraham Lincoln, who nearly beat Al Hudaiba in the Superlative Stakes next time; subsequently made all in a traditionally strong maiden (7f, good to firm) on that Newmarket card; looks a Group colt in the making and commands respect with further improvement on the cards.

Thrice-raced colt who is the only maiden in this field but is a useful one, having performed well in the Chesham and the Superlative; about only 1l behind Al Hudaiba at Newmarket and now gets a 3lb pull with that rival; first success is not out of the question.

Held on narrowly in 5f maiden at the Curragh for Jack Foley, then ran well over 6f in the Windsor Castle at Royal Ascot (good to firm); may do better still in the right circumstances but doesn't give the impression he's crying out for today's 7f trip; tongue-tie applied.

Two from two, justifying odds of 5-6 at Salisbury both times; did it in clearcut fashion upped to 7f (good to firm) latest, albeit helped by main market rival failing to show his form; goes into deeper waters but his limitations are not yet confirmed; similar profile to Dr Rascal.

RaceName: Free Digital Racecard At raceday-ready.com Handicap
Spotlight: Not at his best lately, but is back off the same mark as when winning at Leicester (1m4f, good) in April; has won three times over this trip including here and has a solid chance if producing anything like his best.

RaceName: Free Digital Racecard At raceday-ready.com Handicap
Spotlight: Losing run up to 15, but has run well to be placed in his last two starts since the blinkers went back on, at Windsor (11.4f, good to firm) last month and at Lingfield (1m5f, AW) 15 days ago; player.

RaceName: Free Digital Racecard At raceday-ready.com Handicap
Spotlight: Won five in a row at around 1m4f on turf/AW for the Charltons between September 2023 and July 2024, but has suffered heavy defeats in all three starts since returning for this yard in May; new headgear combination will need to make a big difference.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Son of Soldier's Call who was much improved from his debut with third of 11 in maiden over C&D eight days ago; he may do better still though has a high draw here.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Pearl Secret gelding; half-brother to five winners, notably Ey Up Its The Boss (7f-1m2f; RPR 93) and Ey Up It's Maggie (5f; RPR 91); dam unraced; the market can guide for this newcomer.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Yet to show any ability in his three runs to date; gelded before beating one in 7f Redcar maiden nine days ago.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 80-1, ninth of 11 in novice at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) on his debut 27 days ago; lots more is needed from this son of Arizona.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 9-2, made an encouraging start with second of six in maiden at Musselburgh (5f, good to firm) four weeks ago; this Ardad colt is open to progress and must enter calculations.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: AMO Racing Limited & Giselle De Aguiar
Spotlight: Son of Persian Force who has shown fair form when placed in 6f Ayr maiden and 6f Pontefract novice this summer, no extra last half furlong on latter occasion having gone keenly in front; a player here dropping back in trip.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Has failed to beat a rival in 6f Carlisle maiden and 5f Catterick novice this summer; it's easy to look elsewhere.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Alkumait filly; well held in 5.5f Wetherby novice and 5f Catterick maiden last month; significantly more is required.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 33-1, last of five in maiden at Brighton (5.5f, good to firm) on her debut last month; this Territories filly needs to take a big step forward.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Sent off 66-1 but shaped with promise when a debut fourth of 11 in maiden over C&D (good to firm) eight days ago; this daughter of Invincible Army needs considering with likely better to come.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Ardad filly who has progressed with each of her three runs, runner-up in 11-runner maiden at Ripon (6f) 27 days ago; holds good form claims; engaged 7:40 Ripon Monday.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Lope Y Fernandez filly; dam, unplaced over 6f/7f (RPR 52), is a half-sister to 5f winner Country Carnival, out of Listed-placed 5f-6f winning half-sister to useful 6f-1m winner Yourartisonfire; in good hands and a considered newcomer, especially if the market vibes are positive.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 50-1, well-held sixth of ten in novice at Thirsk (6f, good to firm) on her debut 27 days ago; plenty more is required from this Soldier's Cally filly.

RaceName: EBF Restricted Maiden Stakes (For Horses In Band D) (EBF Qualifier) (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 18,000 guineas foal, 12,000gns yearling; dam, placed over 9.4f/1m3f AW (RPR 64), is a sister to French Group-placed 7f/1m 2yo winner Rose Bloom; the betting can prove an accurate indicator for this Caturra filly.
Came up short (fourth of six) in this race three years ago and record suggests he's best suited by Listed level; latest effort, in a Chester contest that he'd won twice previously, confirms as much.

Gelded prior to impressive win at Haydock (7f Listed) and respectable fifth at Royal Ascot (6f Group 1) this season; fared best of the runners from off the pace when second to Witness Stand in this contest 12 months ago; top on ratings in this bid to go one better.

Creditable second, conceding weight all round, in 6f AW Group 3 at Newcastle latest start; readily bagged Group 2 honours at Doncaster on last attempt over 7f on home soil and may be capable of further progress at this distance; one of the main contenders.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
Spotlight: Still useful but has failed to back up the form of his Irish Group 2 success two years ago and finished behind some of today's rivals in last three outings; losing sequence looks set to be extended.

Prevailed in Group 3 event at York (7f, good) last time, bouncing back to form with tongue-tie fitted (retained today) and dropped back in trip; record of 3-3 at Goodwood features a success when pacemaker in last year's Sussex Stakes; commands respect returned to this venue.

Progressive handicapper who landed the Hunt Cup from favourable draw at Royal Ascot (1m, good to firm) most recently; faces a stiffer task on these terms but possibly hasn't reached his ceiling yet and a strike-rate of 5-6 over 7f bodes well.

Best effort this year when going close in Group 3 at Epsom on penultimate start; record at Goodwood features two wins at this meeting, including in this race 12 months ago, and a good second to Qirat on worse terms in a handicap; shortlist material back here.

Has progressive AW form, notably winning twice at Kempton; possibly flattered by his bare figure when rank outsider in Group 1 at Royal Ascot last time; in any case, needs to find further improvement.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: March foal by Minzaal; 75,000gns yearling, 160,000gns breeze-up 2yo; half-brother to winners Atomic Force (5f/6f including 2yo Group 2; RPR 112), Inexorable Tide (1m/8.6f AW; 85), Dansing Bear (1m4f AW; 68) and Wilsons Ruby (6f-1m including 2yo/AW); dam 10.5f winner (90); nice pedigree and market should be revealing on debut.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 260,000gns yearling; sent off a weak 17-2 shot for his Windsor debut (6f, good to firm) 15 days ago, but ran well to be beaten under a length into second of the 12 runners; shouldn't have a problem with the extra furlong and very much respected.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: April foal by Showcasing; 35,000gns foal, 60,000gns yearling; half-brother to winners Air To Air (7f/1m; RPR 103) and Walson's Law (7f/1m; 91); dam unplaced 6f-8.5f (46), half-sister to 1m2f Group 2 winner Air Pilot, out of 1m6f winner; something to like on breeding and stable does have the occasional winning 2yo newcomer; market useful.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: March foal by Frankel; first foal; dam 7f/1m winner (including 2yo/AW/dirt/Listed; RPR 110), closely related to useful 1m2f/11.5f winner Soft Winds, out of 1m2f/11.4f winning half-sister to Group 2 winners Policy Maker (1m4f) and Pushkin (1m6f); plenty to like on breeding and the stable's record both here and with 2yos first time out make him worthy of respect.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Gradually getting there and was having his third start when beaten a head at Windsor (6f, good to firm) 15 days ago; may improve again, but Mithaaly recorded a much quicker time when runner-up in the other division; further progress needed.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: March foal by Soldier's Call; 33,000gns foal, 65,000gns yearling; half-brother to six winners including Tawdeea (1m-1m4f including AW; RPR 109), Alward (1m1f-1m2f including Australia; 98) and Shadal (1m-9.5f including 2yo/AW/Australia; 83); dam 1m2f winner (93), half-sister to 1m4f Group 2 winner Maraahel; enough to like on breeding and the market should reveal what is expected.

RaceName: 30 Years Of The Hurn Racing Club EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: 600,000gns yearling by Too Darn Hot; 2l third of nine at Lingfield (AW) on debut this month (7f; more experienced Romanza was second); closely related to a very useful turf performer; major contender.

RaceName: 30 Years Of The Hurn Racing Club EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Stradavarius half-brother to four winners at up to 1m1f, one Group-placed in Germany; bought for 140,000euros as a yearling; interesting newcomer.

RaceName: 30 Years Of The Hurn Racing Club EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: Best run when 4.5l seventh of 14 in the Chesham in June (7f, good to firm); fair second at Lingfield (AW) next time but not sure to confirm that form with third-placed Apulia Bay, who was making his debut.

RaceName: 30 Years Of The Hurn Racing Club EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Spotlight: By Lucky Vega; 68,000euros yearling; beaten only 1.5l when fourth of five in an Ayr novice on debut 15 days ago (7f, good to firm; 5-2); should improve.

Two wins here in May initiated his tremendous progress last season; flopped at odds-on when he was rather forced to make the running in Yorkshire Cup on 2026 reappearance, but he ran on nicely for a creditable sixth of 12 in a very strong Hardwicke at Royal Ascot (1m4f) next time; stays 1m6f and has each-way claims if he gets this new trip.

Smart performer on his day, as when a 1m6f handicap winner at 2025 Royal Ascot and again on two of three starts this season; beaten a neck by Illinois in 2m5f Queen Alexandra back at Royal Ascot on latest; however, he managed only fifth in this race last year and this renewal also looks tough.

OwnerName: Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier & Michael Tabor
Spotlight: 7l second to Trawlerman in 2025 Gold Cup at Royal Ascot and beaten three-quarters of a length by Scandinavia in this; those performances were near his best but most since have been pretty grim; this season's clear exception was when he made class tell with sights lowered in the 2m5f Queen Alexandra at Royal Ascot, winning by a neck from French Master, but latest start showed again that today's task is likely to take him well out of his comfort zone.

Second last term in the Derby and third in the Irish Derby; not seen afterwards as a 3yo but 2m races at Sandown this season have seen his promise renewed for serious stamina tests; it was just a four-runner Listed race last time when he dominated from the front at 4-7, so he needs much better today, but cheekpieces are enlisted and he's a fascinating newcomer to a top staying race.

Two clashes with Scandinavia last term (Royal Ascot and the St Leger) indicated there was little between them and he returned with an authoritative win in the Yorkshire Cup at York in May; all three of those races were over about 1m6f and, having turned for home in fourth when 8-1 in the 2m4f Gold Cup at Royal Ascot, he ended up beaten 24l in eighth; now tries his hand at 2m and maybe he'll get it, but others have proved their stamina.

OwnerName: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: Unbeaten with cheekpieces added for his last six starts, including this race last year (outbattled an in-form Illinois), the St Leger at Doncaster (by a neck from Rahiebb) that September and last month's 2m4f Gold Cup at Royal Ascot; had proven fitness on his side against the reappearing Trawlerman when inching ahead close home in their magnificent duel for the Gold Cup, but his stayers' crown is unlikely to be relinquished without a mighty effort whatever the circumstances.

Can make the running (he doesn't have to) to maximise the emphasis on stamina; won a handicap at this meeting in 2022 in his only appearance at Goodwood and has battled it out in the top staying contests since autumn 2023; unbeaten in four British races last season, but reappearance this term was delayed until his repeat bid for the Gold Cup at Royal Ascot and he lost out to Scandinavia in only the dying strides; he didn't look far off his best that day but there's clearly an argument that he will have come on from the run.

Suited by step up to 2m when Listed winner on final start last term and she's played creditable supporting roles in Group events this term; best form when 11l fifth at 80-1 behind Scandinavia and Trawlerman in the 2m4f Gold Cup at Royal Ascot last time; needs to find extra and headgear is given a go.

RaceName: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap
Spotlight: Had fallen 6lb below his sole winning mark when beaten a length into second of seven over C&D (good to firm) this month; drops into a 0-55 for the first time and he's high on list.

RaceName: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap
Spotlight: Made an encouraging return from six months off when third of six behind an in-form rival at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) 11 days ago; down another 1lb and although shorter trips may suit her better, she still makes more appeal than most.

RaceName: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap
Spotlight: Latest fifth of nine in a 0-50 classified event at Lingfield (1m, AW; first-time visor) was probably better than it looks, but he has finished unplaced in all 11 starts so something extra will be needed.

RaceName: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap
Spotlight: Three-time course winner over 6f-1m including twice last summer; best effort since when runner-up to a thriving rival in a 0-50 classified over C&D (soft) last month; inconsistent, but still worth considering.

RaceName: Download The Raceday Ready App Handicap
Spotlight: 0-20 and best form (such as it is) has come on soft ground; moderate in four starts last year and makes little appeal back from nine months off.
Off the mark for the season when winning by a neck at Musselburgh last time (7f, good); could go well again but bit disappointing in only previous run here.
Beat a 1-9 shot in a match at Leicester last month (1m, good to firm), but well-beaten last of 11 in a stronger race at York next time (1m, good to firm); bit to prove.

In good form since 8,000gns buy in April, winning off 5lb lower at Brighton in June (7f, good to firm; 8-11) before a good second to a subsequent winner at Doncaster nine days later (1m, good to firm); contender.
C&D novice winner last August (good to firm); hasn't recaptured her form in three handicaps this season (favourite on first occasion) but returns on a 6lb lower mark having had a wind operation.

OwnerName: Buist, Shields, Thompson And Mrs R Carr
Spotlight: Two of his three wins last year were on fast ground over C&D; well beaten over C&D on belated reappearance two weeks ago; shpuld come on for that.
Won twice last season (6f, good to firm; 7f, soft), although was disappointing on last two runs; hasn't recaptured her form this season; best watched for now.
Ran his best race of the season when close second in a low-grade C&D handicap last time (good to firm); has a stiffer task up in grade here.

Group 1-class sprinter at his best but it's been a struggle this season since an encouraging start at Listed level and he now has his sights lowered for a first crack at a handicap; has a lot of weight and perhaps better at 6f than 5f.

Made all in last season's Ayr Gold Cup (6f, soft) and competes off the same mark here after taking Toby Moore's claim into account; won over 5f at Meydan during the winter and gave it a good shot last time at Ascot (5f); finished fourth in last year's Stewards' Cup so handles this track; respected.

Progressive front-runner who was denied late on in the Dash at Epsom (5f, good to soft; has won on good to firm) in early June; he'll give backers a run for their money but could again be picked off where it matters.

All wins over 6f (on soft and good ground) and he's 0-5 at 5f; can lead; 5lb higher than when winning the Ayr Silver Cup (soft) last September but Jack Callan claims 3lb and forget Ascot last month as he banged his head on the stalls; however, at this trip others are preferred.

Front-runner; 3lb lower than for his runaway win at Haydock last September (5f, good) but hasn't got a lot going in his last four races and was tailed off in Epsom's Dash, in which he was second in 2024; others preferred.

OwnerName: L Bond & Sheikh Aymen Jawad Al Hamandi
Spotlight: Came good off a reduced mark at Doncaster in June (5f, good to firm) but two lesser efforts have followed and this is a tough race in which to bounce back.

Royal Ascot handicap winner last year (5f, good to firm) and later went close in this race when 3lb higher; yet to get competitive this term but could have needed the comeback run, there were blindfold issues next time and she ran well for a long way at Ascot 17 days ago before eased considerably late on; drawn next to the stands' rail and a revival is not out of the question with form figures of 132 under the returning Oisin Murphy; tongue tied last two races.
All three wins and best form have been on the AW, delivering a career high at Newcastle in January (5f AW); lower turf mark sees him 2lb higher here but he is 0-11 on grass and lacks a recent run.
Has added to his impressive tally with two further 5f wins this season but recent defeats suggest others might be on kinder marks.

Last season went well and so too this current campaign for new trainer with 5f wins on good to soft (handles faster) and Tapeta; may not have reached his ceiling just yet and has been third and first in his two runs here.

Back from a break and wind surgery when impressive in a big field at York in May 2024 (5f, good to firm; 7lb lower); however, failed to fire at Meydan this year and was again down the field at Newcastle a month ago; cheekpieces replace a hood.

Classy sprinter back in the day and the new visor has been floating his boat with recent form figures of 121 in 5f handicaps, latterly getting up in the nick of time at Newmarket; only 3lb higher and this hold-up performer should have this run to suit; finished fifth in last year's Stewards' Cup, faring best in his group; firmly in calculations.
Ended a losing run in a Class 4 at Windsor (6f, good to firm) last month but only fourth of seven when penalised at Epsom; well beaten in his two visits here.

Made all at Chester this spring and always prominent when narrowly denied in a small field at Sandown latest (5f, good; second run in cheekpieces); probably worth taking on, with consistency not his forte.
An 8yo mare but as good as ever and close up in 5f handicaps this season at this track, Windsor and Ascot; in the mix.

Novice winner who is threatening to win his first handicap having been denied narrowly this month by Naana's Sparkle and Twilight Calls; a late bump didn't help his cause last time at Newmarket and the visor (on for last three races) is working well; possibilities.

Made the most of a drop in grade to edge home in a Class 4 at York 18 days ago (5f, good to firm) and went up only 3lb for that; however, he's by no means certain to repeat that effort and he lacks course experience.
Yet another prominent racer; in good form since returning from a break but appeared to be beaten fair and square behind some of these at Newmarket's July meeting.

Well beaten in the last two editions of the Stewards' Cup here but won from off the pace over C&D in May, leading on the line under a Jamie Spencer masterclass; barely sighted in his two subsequent runs (soft/AW; ridden more prominently) but, back in this scenario with a strong pace guaranteed, he could easily be a factor if reverting to patient tactics.

Ex-French; didn't get the best of runs when pipped by Seven Questions here in May and overcame some bother in running to go one better at Doncaster last time (5f, good to firm); 4lb rise is fair and this sort of race should suit his style.

Two no-shows at Goodwood were at this meeting in 2023, including this race; however, provided the track doesn't pose any problems, he could be interesting after strong finishes in the Dash at Epsom and last time at Chester where a slow start was the last thing he needed; he should be coming home to some effect.

Played his part in a strong pace last time at York yet hung around to finish a half-length behind winner Ziggy's Triton; has little margin for error off this mark and other pace influences temper enthusiasm.
Disappointing favourite two months ago at Windsor and, although only 3lb higher than when a clearcut winner back in the spring (5f, soft; fine on good), this demands a career best from him.

Exposed ten-time winner who was down the field in this 12 months ago when 1lb higher; won at Ripon this month (no headgear) before finishing fifth of seven 11 days ago at Pontefract (visored); a long time since he wore blinkers.

RaceName: Play At The Races Stableduel Handicap
Spotlight: Well backed when making all and winning easily at the 17th attempt over C&D (good to firm) this month; up 7lb, but a chance he may enjoy his own way again so could be hard to catch if he does.

RaceName: Play At The Races Stableduel Handicap
Spotlight: 14-race maiden when trained in Ireland and was always behind on his stable debut/reappearance at Kempton (7f, AW) in May; off another three months since and has enough to prove, not least stamina.

RaceName: Play At The Races Stableduel Handicap
Spotlight: Off the mark at the 15th attempt in a steadily run race at Newmarket (1m4f, good to firm) last month, but didn't match that form off the same mark at Chepstow (1m4f, good to firm) one week later; needs to bounce back in first-time cheekpieces for last year's winning stable.

RaceName: Play At The Races Stableduel Handicap
Spotlight: Made an encouraging turf debut after 124 days off when fourth of eight at Nottingham (1m2f, good to firm) this month; back off the same mark as when winning at Southwell (1m, AW; 66-1) in January and she's one to be interested in.

RaceName: Play At The Races Stableduel Handicap
Spotlight: Both wins over 1m, at Ffos Las (heavy) last September and at Newcastle (AW) last month; finished second of six at Nottingham (1m2f, good to firm) this month and she is one for the shortlist off the same mark.

RaceName: Play At The Races Stableduel Handicap
Spotlight: 0-19 and finished around 12l behind Divot over C&D (good to firm) last time; hard to warm to.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
OwnerName: D P Van Der Hoeven & D G Pryde
Spotlight: Won three on the trot last season (5f/6f); off the mark for the current year when scoring at Ayr 15 days ago (6f, good to firm); up 3lb; should go well again.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
Spotlight: Won 5f Ayr handicap off 6lb higher in May last year (5f, good to firm) but mainly disappointing since, including on last two starts; bit to prove at present.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
OwnerName: Grange Park Racing XIII & Ruth Carr
Spotlight: Pontefract winner in April (5f, good to soft); two good runs in May, the first when second over this C&D; hasn't been in such good form on last two runs.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
OwnerName: Slaters Arms Racing And Ged Shields
Spotlight: Mainly in good form last season, winning over 6f at Pontefract in June (6f, good); disappointing this season, but now 3lb below his last winning mark.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
Spotlight: Has been rather disappointing since winning off 1lb lower at Ripon in April (6f, good to soft), including in cheekpieces two runs ago (last of 13 at York); effective at 5f; easier ground suits.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
Spotlight: Yet to win on turf, but sound runs when runner-up at Thirsk (5f, good) and Ayr (5f, good to firm) on last two starts; one with a chance.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
Spotlight: Two wins this term, the first at Southwell in April and the second over C&D last week (good to firm); could go well from her low draw, but lacks consistency.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
Spotlight: Three sound runs this term, winning his last two, at Wetherby in June (5.5f, good to firm) and over C&D two weeks ago (good to firm); this looks a stronger race, but he could go well again.

RaceName: It's Ladies Day Next On 12 August Handicap
Spotlight: Dual C&D winner last July (good to firm/soft); yet to hit top form this season, although hasn't been beaten far on last two runs.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Won a bumper in fine style at this meeting last year for Andy Slattery; disappointed in a Leopardstown bumper on debut for this yard in December; much more like it when winning on hurdling debut at Listowel (16.5f, good) latest and the third from that race has won since; big player.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Useful on the Flat and rated 89; made a winning start for this yard over hurdles at Killarney in May (2m1f, gd-yld); heavy defeat in a Punchestown novice on latest too bad to be true (small graze on right-fore cannon bone); no surprise were he to bounce back.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: One of two for yard; 2-3 over hurdles and rated 130; won Punchestown 4yo maiden in mid-May (2m, good); added a 4yo hurdle at Ballinrobe (2m, good) later that month; could be more to come but Jack Kennedy prefers the chances of Lizzie Twigg.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Flat winner; 0-4 over hurdles and rated 103; 1.25l second in Market Rasen maiden hurdle 23 days ago (20.5f, good); cheekpieces go on but surely out of depth in this company; due to run 5.40 here on Monday.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: 0-2 in point-to-points and 0-4 over hurdles; beaten off 82 in Cork handicap hurdle on latest; this looks far too demanding.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Bumper winner; has made a flawless start over hurdles, winning a Punchestown maiden hurdle (16.5f, gd-yld) by 8.25l and a Roscommon novice (2m, good) by 3.5l; unexposed and preferred by Jack Kennedy; obvious chance.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Decent strike rate over fences (3-10) and rated 121; disappointed on sole start over hurdles at Punchestown in April and beaten 5l in Kilbeggan handicap chase on latest; cheekpieces worn that day discarded; others are more persuasive.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
OwnerName: Nicholas Fahy/Mrs Orla Fahy/Two Sheets to the Wind Syndicate
Spotlight: Close second in a Punchestown bumper in January (2m, sft-hvy); justified favouritism to land an ordinary Downpatrick mares' maiden hurdle (2m2f, good) two weeks ago; this is harder but she's unexposed in this sphere so don't discount.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Novice Hurdle (Listed Race)
Spotlight: Runner up in two of four starts in bumpers; filled the same spot on hurdling debut in a mares' maiden at Kilbeggan; this is much tougher.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Ties in with Launch Sequence on debut effort; neck second to unbeaten rival, pair clear, when favourite at Newbury (6f, good to firm) since; may take another step forward; major contender.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Showed ability by leading for long way in big-field event at Newbury (6f, good to firm; finished fifth) but the bare form gives him plenty to find in this festival maiden.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Made no impact in 7f contest at Sandown where he was one of the outsiders; handicaps are likely to be his thing in due course.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 60,000gns yearling; by Showcasing; sibling to three winners, notably Sense Of Duty (6f including 2yo/Group 3; RPR 116); dam 1m scorer (92); one of four newcomers in the field; market instructive.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 55,000gns yearling; by Dark Angel and first foal of 6f AW 2yo winner (RPR 73) whose siblings include 7f/1m 2yo scorer Starlight Time; starts off in a competitive maiden; check the betting.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Twice-raced colt who holds a respectable chance assuming latest effort, namely 125-1 seventh of 25 from unfavourable draw in the Windsor Castle (6f) at Royal Ascot, is backed up.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Similar type to Dorigo, having belied his 125-1 odds with a seemingly good effort over 6f at Royal Ascot (seventh of 21 in the Coventry) last time; hung right that day and gelded since.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 20,000gns yearling; Land Force half-brother to 6f 2yo scorer Gesayed (RPR 77); dam maiden (62), half-sister to a few Listed-placed winners; faces a stiff-looking introduction.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Group 2 Gimcrack entry; very promising and eye-catching third of 11 in novice event (6f, good to firm) at Doncaster, finishing nicely under hands and heels once switched and in the clear (met traffic issues); respected.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 100,000euros yearling, 45,000euros (breeze-up) 2yo; Mehmas half-brother to three winners, notably Gavota (Group-placed 6f/7f 2yo; RPR 105); dam unraced; yard landed this race with a newcomer in 2017; interesting.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Showed some promise with fourth of 11 at Thirsk (6f) and may be able to win a race, perhaps in the north; however, has a lot to find in this warm maiden, sent down south.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Holds two major Group entries; solid second, behind the subsequent Albany winner, at Leicester; combination of drop to 5f and meeting trouble seemingly contributed to a poor effort at Royal Ascot; remains of interest.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Finished 6l seventh in Listed event at Newbury (6f, good to firm; 66-1) where he was the sole newcomer in a field of ten; interesting dropped in class, with improvement plausible.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Twice-raced colt whose opening mark of 71 reflects that his form claims are ordinary kept to maiden level today, rather than switching to a nursery; looked ill at ease on the Epsom track last time.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Has some ability but his two efforts suggest nurseries will be more suitable shortly; certainly needs improvement in this deep maiden.

RaceName: British Stallion Studs EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings) (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Needs to improve markedly on the form he showed in a big field at Newbury (6f).

RaceName: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Three wins have come over 6f/7f, but he was beaten only a neck by Nymphaea in a 0-50 apprentice classified event at Nottingham (1m2f, good to firm) a week ago; attempts this far for the first time, but still a player on that latest performance.

RaceName: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Seemed to win with a bit more in hand than the margin would suggest when beating Charencey by a neck in a 0-50 apprentice classified event at Nottingham (1m2f, good to firm) one week ago; stamina not in doubt over this longer trip having won over 1m6f at the same track last month; high on the list.

RaceName: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Running well lately, chasing home a subsequent winner at Epsom (1m4f, good) last time; losing run is up to 17, though, so she may again find one or two too good.

RaceName: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Completed a hat-trick in the middle of last year, but 0-11 since despite a plummeting mark; needs a resurgence.

RaceName: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Has run well on good to firm, but looks best on a softer surface; either way a record of 2-49 sounds a note of caution; stable won this last year.

RaceName: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Classified Stakes
OwnerName: Hambleton Racing Lvi & Mrs G Jarvis
Spotlight: Five-race maiden who showed a bit more when third of seven in a similar contest at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) three weeks ago; runner-up has won since, but she still has something to prove back up in trip.

RaceName: Winning Experience With Moulton Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 0-8; not disgraced when third of seven in a similar contest over C&D (good to firm) 13 days ago, but will need to do better again if he is to make an impact.
1-13 and rated 117 over hurdles; below best in that sphere in 2026 and moderate run in Flat maiden at Killarney on latest; best watched on chase debut.
Won just one of twelve starts in point-to-points; unseated in both previous starts under Rules; hard to make a case for.

Very useful over hurdles (5-18, rated 147); goes on any ground and should be sharper for his latest run in a Grade 3 hurdle at Limerick after an 87 day break; every chance he'll take to this game on breeding; big player on chase debut.

One of three for yard; 1-6 over hurdles and rated 121; promising start over fences when a 2.75l third at Wexford (2m7f,gd-yld); soundly beaten over 19.5f (good) back there on latest, overlooked by Townend and this trip may be on the sharp side.

Point-to-point winner; scored in a bumper at this meeting last year; 1-8 over hurdles and rated 137; half-brother to two chase winners and dam a half-sister to high-class chaser Empire Of Dirt; acts on good ground and interesting on chase debut.

One of three for yard; bumper winner; 2-6 over hurdles and rated 135; has come up short in graded hurdles on last four starts; dam a useful chaser so could take to this discipline; tongue tie goes on; not discounted.

Novice hurdle winner here in October 2024 (20.5f, soft); lightly raced since; sent off the 6-4 favourite in this last year on return from 234 days off and found just one too good; similar preparation this year and Townend keeps the faith; player.
Useful dual-purpose performer; rated 83 on the Flat; 1-6 over hurdles and rated 127; out of form on the Flat this year, however, and not bred for chasing; others appeal more.

0-3 in point-to-points; 2-6 and rated 117 over hurdles; promising start to chasing career when runner up at Wexford; blotted copybook when unseating at the first back there on latest; probably up against it in this company.
2-18 over hurdles; rated 114 after two chase starts; rallied well for a close second in Punchestown novice chase on latest (20.5f, gd-yld); more needed dropped in trip.

Both wins over 1m2f on good to firm ground, the latest a narrow success (on her second start for this yard) at Newbury last month; beaten less than a length into fourth of nine at Ascot (1m, good to firm) 17 days ago; back up 1lb and this sharper track is not sure to be in her favour.

Has a good strike-rate (4-9) including two Group wins at San Siro (1m, good); twice held since returning to home soil, latest when midfield in the Sandringham at Ascot (1m, good to firm) last month; 2lb drop is not enough to tempt.

Defied a lengthy absence when winning at Doncaster (1m, good to firm) last month and then ran a fine race to finish fifth of 24 in the Kensington Palace at Ascot (1m, good to firm), especially as she met traffic; could have been better drawn, but she races off the same mark as last time and represents last year's winning stable; shortlisted.

Landed a Leicester novice (7f, good) and a Newcastle handicap (1m, AW) last autumn; solid efforts in her first two starts this term, but was a bit disappointing at Newmarket (7f, good to firm) 17 days ago; drawn high and needs to get back on track.

Seen only three times since winning a Kempton novice (1m, AW) in October 2024; hasn't shown enough in two starts this season to suggest she will be winning a race as competitive as this, albeit with a hood now given a go.

Has completely taken off lately, completing the hat-track when winning at Newbury (7f, good to firm); up another 6lb, but that latest form has been boosted by the subsequent wins of the second and fourth (twice); well drawn and very likely to make her presence felt; yard won this in 2021.

Won four times last year and was beaten less than a length into second of nine at Chester (7.5f, good; goes well there) 17 days ago; admirable sort, but looks weighted to her best and may prove vulnerable to younger rivals.

Placed in all three starts over 7f late last year, firstly at Kempton (AW) and then twice at Meydan (dirt); clearly has ability, but has questions to answer on turf/handicap debut after 221 days off; market may help.

Chased home this season's smart Inis Mor at Newmarket (7f, good to soft) in sole start as a 2yo and did well at Southwell (1m, AW) early this year, winning a maiden and going down narrowly under a penalty in a novice; makes her handicap debut after 167 days off; stable won this in 2024; watch market.
Took nine attempts to get off the mark but now bids for a hat-trick after two wins at Chester (7.5f; soft/good); up another 5lb but still one for the shortlist now that something has clearly clicked.

3-29, the latest win coming at Lingfield (1m1f, good) a year ago; still 3lb higher and although she may appreciate the return to turf, she looks vulnerable to less exposed rivals; stable also runs Perdy In Paris.

Has progressed in each of her three starts, making all in a Carlisle novice (1m, good to firm) latest; it's not clear how strong the form is, but she is bred to useful and respected on handicap debut despite her high draw.

Made a winning reappearance in Doncaster maiden (7f, good to firm) in April, but only fourth of eight when favourite for handicap debut at Windsor (1m, good to firm; started slowly) the following month; has a bit to find from the same mark and is drawn wide; stable won this in 2018 and 2020.

Placed on AW in all three starts, the latest when second of 14 in a Kempton maiden (7f) in May after six-month absence; returns from another break and looks a stiff task on handicap/turf debut from 3lb out of the weights.
Both wins came over C&D last year and has dropped 5lb lower than for the latest in September; modest effort at Southwell (7f, AW) last time, but still of interest returned to this track.

Had his ideal combination of fast ground and a strong pace when back to winning form at Doncaster (7f, good to firm) ten days ago; only 2lb higher and much respected if this pans out in a similar way, which looks a possibility.
Went up 5lb for winning a match over C&D (soft) last month and was well held off this mark at Nottingham (1m, good to firm) last time; others look better treated.
Better effort when fourth of ten at Thirsk (7f, good to firm) this month and now 2lb below his last winning mark, but he is just 1-42 in Britain.

Ran three times as a 2yo for Karl Burke before moving to Ireland, where he won a handicap at Dundalk (7f, AW) in March; makes his debut for last year's winning stable having changed hands for 6,000gns this month; market useful.

Front-runner who has dropped 1lb lower than when winning a handicap at Newcastle (7f, Tapeta) for Richard Fahey last November, but will need to show a lot more than when tailed off on stable debut at Southwell (1m, AW) in March.

Eight-race maiden who has been a bit in and out since handicapping and the removal of the hood (still missing) made no difference when third of four at Lingfield (6f, good to firm) last time; needs a bit more.
0-7; hasn't built on the promise she showed on a couple of occasions last year and the application of a tongue-tie has made little difference; best watched.

OwnerName: The Boys Are Back In Town
Spotlight: 0-8; finished second of five on nursery debut here (1m, good to soft) last September, but well beaten in four outings since; cheekpieces return.

Has won over hurdles but 0-8 in chases and yet to trouble the judge; beaten 33l in 2m Punchestown handicap chase on latest; drops in grade, steps up in trip and cheekpieces go on; needs more for last year's winning stable.

In excellent form since return from long layoff; won over hurdles at Kilbeggan in April; added a Cartmel handicap chase (17.5f, good) last month; this is tougher, however, so will need a career best to follow up.

Two-time winner over timber, including at this venue last September (16.5f, gd-yld); 0-5 over fences but hasn't run badly the last twice (trip too far on latest) and the handicapper is giving him a chance; likes it here and not dismissed.

One of three for stable; flat and hurdles winner off the mark over fences off 6lb lower at Wexford (2m, gd-yld) when last seen in May; this longer trip should be fine and yard made hay at this meeting last season; can't discount.

1-12 over hurdles; posted a solid effort on chase debut in a beginners' at Wexford (19.5f, good) last month, keeping on from the back for a 4.5l second of 14; not obviously well treated for handicap chase bow but not written off.

5-33 over fences and arrives on the back of successive front running 19.5f wins at Downpatrick, both on good ground; has gone up a total of 13lb but clearly in good heart and should make another bold bid here.

OwnerName: Ed Mulligan & John Finnegan & Aileen Saunders & Ann Holton
Spotlight: Point winner scored in a handicap chase at Ayr in December (16.5f, heavy); pulled up behind Finnians Row at Downpatrick on latest; may need softer ground than this.

2-9 over fences; won off 12lb lower at Clonmel in January (2m, heavy) and off 6lb lower at Tramore (15.5f, yielding) in April; not beaten far off 2lb lower at Wexford (2m, gd-yld) on latest; return to a right-handed track a plus; stays this far and in the mix.

Two-time hurdles winner; his good second over fences at Roscommon in June (16.5f, yielding) would give him a chance here but didn't back it up at Wexford and failed to fire back over hurdles at Killarney on latest.
Two wins over hurdles for Gavin Cromwell; 0-7 over fences and has a tendency to jump left at times; ground conditions will suit but soundly beaten over hurdles on latest and others make more appeal.
Veteran; 1-18 over fences, the win coming on testing ground at Listowel in September 2024; out of form when last seen in February and remains 4lb above that last success; others appeal more.

Point to point winner has yet to make much of an impact under Rules; well held in beginners' chase at Wexford on latest (behind Ned In The Park); previously pulled up in handicap chase at Tramore; in good hands but much more needed.

Promise in all three chase starts, including when a 2.5l second behind Giant Haystacks in a handicap at Wexford on latest despite not jumping fluently at times; nudged up 2lb and this is tougher but could go well if jumping better.
Winning hurdler yet to make much impression over the bigger obstacles; remote second at Bangor in May her best effort but soundly beaten at Hexham on latest; needs more.

One of three for yard; sent off favourite and rewarded backers with a first win over fences at Wexford (19.5f, good) on latest, beating A Snow White Park by 2.5l; 6lb higher now and steps up in grade but should go well again.

One of three for yard; off the mark over fences in a Downpatrick beginners (19.5f, gd-yld) in May (Giant Haystacks 2.75l behind in fourth); unseated two out in handicap chase back there on latest when still in contention; can't discount off 2lb higher.

Won off 3lb lower at Thurles (18.5f, yielding) in November; struggled on next three starts but step in right direction when a 5l third of seven at Wexford on latest (15.5f, good, jockey dropped whip after two out); eased 1lb and this longer trip more suitable.

Three-time winning hurdler; 2-13 in chases, his last win coming over 2m6f (good) at Thurles in January 2025 off 9lb higher; hinted at a return to form when staying on for a remote fourth at Wexford latest (2m, good); on a dangerous mark and this longer trip will suit.

Won over hurdles at Downpatrick (2m2f, good) in May and rated 8lb higher in that sphere; 0-4 over fences but has shown potential, including when a 6.5l third at Wexford in June; runner up over hurdles on latest; more needed back over fences.

Winning hurdler is 0-11 over fences; ran okay in handicap chases over further at Clonmel and Wexford earlier this year but seems best with cut in the ground; beaten 22l on good ground in a handicap hurdle on latest.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Career win number ten when scooting clear in a Class 3 fillies' handicap at Newmarket in early May and she ran in a Listed race next time; however, she went up 12lb for that last win and looks vulnerable off this mark.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Highly tried after winning her novice in 2024, confined to Listed and Group races ever since; it's difficult to gauge where she is right now and cheekpieces are turned to.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Won the 3yo Dash at Epsom (5f, good) last term and fourth in the older-horse version this season; just as effective at 6f and she never got a chance to show her true colours last time at Chester; lacking course experience is not ideal but she's not dismissed.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Won three sprints last year on extremes of going; however, a near-miss at Listed level in April put paid to her handicap mark and others look better treated.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Maiden/novice wins at 6f; ran okay to be ninth of 27 on handicap debut at Royal Ascot (5f, good to firm; second favourite) before flying too high in a Group 3 at Sandown, again wandering under pressure; not yet exposed and she's returning to what is probably her best trip; wears first-time tongue-tie and cheekpieces; interesting.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: First-time cheekpieces and a reduced mark when coming good again at Ripon (6f, good) in May and she was close up in Bintaryana's race at York next time; the latter form in particular raises hopes but she was off her game last time at Pontefract.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
OwnerName: Ms H N Pinniger And Partner
Spotlight: Close up over C&D in June (soft) and gained her first win away from Windsor when challenging 1f out and just holding on at Salisbury (6f, good to firm) on latest start; 2lb rise is no big deal but this race is way deeper.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Made debut over 1m; confined to 7f since, winning minor races at Chester and Wetherby before bumping into what looked a handicap snip at Newmarket's July meeting (good to firm; this filly was sent off favourite); looks quick enough for 6f and has to be feared for a flying-high stable.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Won her novice over C&D (good) for William Haggas whom she left for 6,000gns; that looks a bargain after she emerged from last to first when denying Shallow over 6f at Newmarket 11 days ago; that was quite taking and she could still be nicely treated off 5lb higher.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: York handicap winner last season and overcame a wide draw at Chester in May (6f, good; 4lb lower); good and bad since, though saw too much daylight when returned to 7f at Newmarket last time (behind Machadadorp); better can be expected, assuming she copes with this new experience.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Often leads; ran in a Listed race in May but underwhelming handicap efforts since on Newmarket's July course and she usually runs that track well; needs a revival and she's unraced here.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Races prominently; behind some of these in a 7f handicap at the Newmarket July meeting but the visor went on back there 11 days ago and, in a 6f handicap she'd won the previous year, she beat all bar late player Sing The Blues; her close third behind Bintaryana at York in June is another key piece of form that heightens interest.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: It was over 7f that she won at the Newmarket July meeting but she raced freely off steady fractions there and won her novice at this trip; 1lb lower than last time if taking into account Ashley Lewis's claim and this improving filly could yet rate higher.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Highly tried last season after winning her maiden; back on track in just her second handicap when prevailing by a length in second-time cheekpieces at Carlisle (6f, good to firm); it could be onwards and upwards from there and she took only a 3lb hit.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Promise in defeat last season; won a Ripon novice by 7l in May (6f, good; first-time cheekpieces) and followed up in a three-runner handicap at Salisbury (6f, good to firm; one of her rivals lost all chance at the start); it's hard to rate that form highly and she's 6lb higher, but this well-related filly could have a whole lot more to offer for shrewd connections.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: All the better for blinkers going on in recent starts but she ran only last Friday when beaten fair and square off this mark at Ascot (5f); there are no guarantees that returning to 6f will see her to better effect.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Ran just once at two and firmly on the upgrade this season, leading late on to win at York in mid-June (6f, good; unraced on firmer) in her second handicap; that narrow verdict was a blessing as she's only 2lb higher; would appreciate some give in the ground, according to her trainer, but dangerously unexposed if conditions are suitable.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
OwnerName: Middleham Park Racing Lxxiv & M Hulin
Spotlight: First run after wind surgery when winning easily at Pontefract in April but no further improvement has been forthcoming; returning to 6f is probably no bad thing but others are more intriguing.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Has won handicaps this year at 6f (good to firm) and 7f (AW); similar chance to Shallow on last month's Newmarket clash and the leaders never came back when third from off the pace at Chester latest (6f, good); each-way shout.

RaceName: World Pool Bet With The tote EBF Fillies' Handicap
Spotlight: Five-time winner having a consistent season but her handicap mark hasn't really gone anywhere despite several placed efforts over 5f in lower-grade races than this; has won over this far but the chances are she'll come up short once again.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Didn't look to enjoy the Brighton experience last time, but his small-field selling second previously didn't amount to much anyway (Jazzy Bay third); trainer does much better with 2yos on the AW than turf and he'll need to improve now handicapping.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Nothing exciting in three 6f starts round Windsor, latterly when said to have hung left late on; stable having a quiet year thus far (0-23 with 2yos) and he'll need to improve for the extra furlong.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Disappointing in a seller last time (second run at that level) and the visor goes back on tonight; trainer among the winners and his strike-rate with 2yos is up a touch this season but he's looking exposed now.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Run to a similar level all four starts, incuding behind Parading in a seller in May; didn't look to have any excuses on his nursery debut last time but coming back up from 6f won't hurt.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Showed enough in three runs in the spring to think she can be a factor at this level now handicapping; goes on the shortlist for her much in-form trainer.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Trainer back among the winners and got on the board for the year with 2yos recently (nursery newcomer); he does well with juveniles here too and this filly, who ran green on debut before pulling hard second time, is open to improvement.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Backward step at Newbury last time but has stamina on her dam's side and the extra furlong may help now handicapping off a lowly opening mark; holds each-way claims from the outside stall.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Done most racing over 5f, didn't look to see out 6f in one try, has hung both ways and is looking exposed; cheekpieces go back on and he doesn't make obvious appeal.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Not looked the easiest thus far and goes without the cheekpieces again having not seen out a stiffer 7f last time; trainer 0-27 with 2yos this season and it wouldn't say much for the others were she able to take this.

RaceName: Support Our Local On-Course Bookmakers Nursery Handicap
Spotlight: Big prices for three runs to date (5f-6f) last month and finished a well-beaten last each time; trainer 0-24 with 2yos for the season and a shock were he the one to put him on the board.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Finished first in a barrier trial; excellent effort in a maiden at Cork (6f, good) when beaten 1.2l into second by subsequent Group 3 winner Ballinea Star; overall form of the race is possibly suspect.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 66-1, always at the back first time out in a maiden at Leopardstown 12 days ago.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Well held by Argentarius on Cork running; never involved at Leopardstown on second outing.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 550,000gns yearling; eighth foal; Wootton Bassett filly is a half-sister to three winners, including a Group 3 scorer in France; dam a Group-placed winner by Sea The Stars, half-sister to dual French Classic winner Lope De Vega; apprentice aboard for debut.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Zoustar filly; dam 7f winner, sister to 1m2f Group 1 winner Laganore; no match for the smart Folsom Blues (subsequent Group 3 runner-up) on soft ground at Gowran in June; Shane Foley on Samnina.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
OwnerName: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
Spotlight: Apprentice-ridden when 5l third of eight in a maiden at Listowel in May; form of that race has been boosted by runner-up Big Negotiator; picked up valuable experience when third in a 7f maiden at Newmarket 19 days ago; winner Scommessa Secura can be rated a useful yardstick.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Only 1/2l behind subsequent winner Livenka when fourth on debut at the Curragh, a race won stylishly by Alpha who scrambled home at short odds in a Group 3 race at Leopardstown last week; promising.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Saxon Warrior filly; made a satisfactory debut in taking third behind the well-fancied Livenka on debut at Fairyhouse; just lost second to Star Of State who has since won a Leopardstown maiden with the greatest of ease; winner's form also linked to Samnina.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E350,000 yearling; sixth foal; half-sister by Too Darn Hot to three winners, including the Group-placed Villanova Queen; dam unraced half-sister to 1m Group 1 (Sussex Stakes) winner Here Comes When.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E380,000 yearling; seventh foal; half-sister by Zarak to four winners; dam unraced half-sister to 5f Group 2 winner Muthmir.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: Stable's second-string now, as on her first two starts; will need a handicap mark.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: E52,000 yearlong, E80,000 Breeze Up; fourth foal; half-sister by Bayside Boy to a seven-time winner in France; dam was a Listed winner in France and Germany.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Irish EBF Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
Spotlight: 65,000gns yearling; eighth foal; sister to Group 2 winner Wonderful Moon, half-sister to four winners; trainer also runs two who have form in the book.

Made a winning debut in 7f Salsibury novice in July 2024; lightly raced since but has posted good third placings in 1m handicaps at Newbury and Yarmouth this summer; very much one to consider off same mark.
Gained a first win at the third attempt in 7f Chepstow maiden in July; last of ten on handicap debut at Newbury (1m) 11 days ago; lots more is needed in a first-time tongue-tie.
Starman filly who is much improved of late, building on Windsor second with breakthrough success in seven-runner handicap over C&D 29 days ago; up 3lb but she merits serious consideration.
Got off the mark at the ninth attempt over C&D last August; yet to hit top form this summer, although saddle reportedly slipped when sixth of eight over C&D four weeks ago; not out of things.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Four-time winner at 7f/1m, the last two at Listed level over 1m on heavy ground in the Knockaire Stakes at Leopardstown, the scene of his best form; beaten only a neck in this race two years ago, tenth behind Dunum last year; drawn low.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Won 2025 Irish Cambridgeshire for Dermot Weld, beating today's rival Genuine Article by a short head; maintained his good record in races over 1m when an emphatic winner from stablemate Far Form Dandy at Naas on seasonal/stable debut; mid-division in the Royal Hunt Cup, seventh of 20 in his group, not a bad effort.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Enjoyed a terrific spell last October, notching three wins and two places during a hectic spell; maintained his rate of improvement when beating 24 rivals in the Irish Lincoln on return; early-season form also included second in a 1m2f premier handicap at the Curragh; unplaced twice in Listed races this term; handicap form gives him a leading chance; drawn low.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Completed a four-timer when winning a 7f handicap here in 2022; won the 7f Ahonoora Handicap at the 2023 festival; made it three from six at this venue (also placed three times) when winning this event last year; third in the Ahonoora later that week; absent since last September; stiff task against that background, despite his liking for the track.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Won on debut at Dundalk in 2024; ran well in top handicaps last season, including third in Victoria Cup at Ascot and second in Ahonoora over 7f at this venue; has taken a while to hit form this season; opened his turf account last month at the 15th attempt; up 7lb for that 7f Cork success.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Ran against smart Ballydoyle colts as a juvenile; won a three-runner 1m conditions event at Naas in March; did not quite see out the extended 1m2f when third in the Prix Noailles at Longchamp; failed to run to expectations in a valuable Gowran contest; could make a high-class handicapper, but no horse of his age has won this since 2004; cheekpieces added.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Seven-time winner, including Listed and Group 3 races; not a bad effort (seventh behind Pierre Royal at the Curragh) on first handicap start since 2023; towards the back at Leopardstown last time; cheekpieces tried.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: No win on turf since September 2024; has run well in defeat in good handicaps this season, including fourth to Ribee in Irish Lincoln; also second to stablemate Jagged Edge at Naas; below-par last time in a Curragh race dominated by Pierre Royal and Booyea; drawn low.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Won a Gowran maiden (1m, good) for Dermot Weld last May; met trouble in running on stable/seasonal debut in a Limerick race won by Monvoe; improved from that when beating Booyea in a 1m premier handicap at the Curragh a month ago; up 9lb, might struggle to confirm form with Booyea (up 5lb).

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Last win was in a valuable 1m handicap at the Curragh in June 2024; best run in almost a year when second to Pierre Royal in the same Curragh event a month ago; should come into the reckoning on that evidence, though 5lb higher now, with the winner up 9lb.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Won the Irish Lincoln last season; attempted to bring off the double at Doncaster and produced a fine effort to finish third of 22 behind Godwinson; has failed to prosper since third to Dunum in this last year; however, he is 8lb lower now and should be at peak fitness after a Curragh prep-run in a race dominated by Pierre Royal and Booyea.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Only two wins from 22 Flat starts; however, he won a C&D handicap 12 months ago, and has been placed nine times; below best on seasonal debut at the Curragh in April; more like it when fifth at the same venue in May; drawn high.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Has done most of her racing at 1m, odds-on for her sole win in a Killarney maiden last autumn; more recent form over longer distances in good company; this is closer to her optimum.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Ended 2025 with a pair of heavy-ground wins at Doncaster (7f); useful form in defeat this year, in the frame in competitive York handicaps (good ground) on consecutive days last month; another good run when fifth of 17 on quick going at the same venue last time; ground-versatile, trip a worry.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Won on good ground at two in France; ran only twice for William Haggas in 2024; same last year for this stable, the best of those a second at Leopardstown on the first of two late-season handicap outings; dismal form in three subsequent outings

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
OwnerName: Just The Two Of Us Partnership
Spotlight: Last of five wins was in 2023 when he ran well in a Group 3 at Leopardstown and a Listed contest at Killarney; not the force he was, though he has run well from time to time, including when sixth of 14 at 80-1 in this race last year; fair third at Killarney last time; valuable 5lb claimed, could go well at a decent price.

RaceName: COLM QUINN BMW Mile Handicap (Premier Handicap)
Spotlight: Has failed to deliver on initial promise as a hurdler; out of his depth in top juvenile events; excuse for failure to take advantage of drop in class at Ballinrobe; won over an extended 7f in France at three; never out of the first three in six races; apart from one AW run, all Flat form on soft or worse; drawn high.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 0-21 before he won a classified at Chepstow (1m, good to firm) four days ago; he'd been knocking on the door with four seconds in his preceding five races this summer, including twice after six-day absences; concedes 5lb all round today but most of the others have been struggling.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: 16-race maiden who has some modest form (mostly on AW) but was beaten 38l and 30l this month in his two starts for new stable; at least this drop back in trip looks a plus.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
OwnerName: Dixon, Wylam, M Baldry, J&s Harrod
Spotlight: Still capable of modest form on occasions last year, including two 1m wins on Southwell AW, but competitive only once (penultimate start) in 2026.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Hampered and unseated on latest start; second in a 7.3f classified here the time before and had a turf win last July, with plenty of occasions too in which he's not been far away, so has each-way claims.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Three wins in an industrious 2025 and another this March; three of those were AW, as was the respectable show in first-time cheekpieces on latest start, while last June's 1m classified win at Chepstow was on soft; others look more solid these days on today's likely good or good to firm ground.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Ex-Irish (1m1f winner in 2024); running for this yard since December and the odd piece of that form gives him a shout, including penultimate start but that was on soft ground; below form sole start on firmer than good.

RaceName: Cymru Bet/Alan Bushell Racing Classified Stakes
Spotlight: Hasn't shown much over jumps and same story this year switched to the Flat; keeps being slowly away and refused to race here on penultimate appearance, admittedly without her usual hood, but still hard to fancy.

Dual AW winner; highlight of British form when second to Big Evs in a Listed race at York in May 2024; rated 99 at his peak. gained his first turf success off 72 when making all in a 20-runner contest at the Curragh three starts ago; now 10lb higher.

OwnerName: Ian O'Connor & The Fox And Hounds
Spotlight: Only one pound higher than when winning at last year's festival; had the same high draw then, so should not be ruled out; has to bounce back from a below-par Salisbury run; previous fourth placings at Doncaster and Thirsk were respectable; had the same high draw last year.

Nine-time turf winner, including a 6f Group 3 in 2023; has also won at Listed level and was once rated 108, so has dropped a long way; inconsistent in recent years; has run well in two sprint handicaps at the Curragh lately.
