Consistent form last year; won at Killarney's July fixture and ended the campaign with seconds at Leopardstown and Dundalk; raced too keenly when stepped up in trip on reappearance at Roscommon a month ago; probably best at 1m.
Has recorded three of his seven wins at Listowel and also twice successful over C&D; out of form before signs of a revival at Limerick last month; still looks risky.

Only win from 23 starts came on heavy ground at Gowran last September; failed to retrieve her best form in her first four outings this term; placed twice (7f/1m1f) at Leopardstown since then, both races run on soft; stamina stretched by 1m2f at the Curragh a month ago.

OwnerName: F J Carragher/Yorkavenue Syndicate/Park Ave Syndicate
Spotlight: Only one win from 27 starts and that was on AW for Brian Meehan in 2023; fair AW form early this year and showed that a turf win could be within his range when second to Dancing Saxon at Limerick last time; form given a big boost by the winner in a Listed race; handicap mark reduced by a stone over the past 12 months; may come good now from low draw..

Four-time AW winner, sole turf success came in 5f handicap at Naas in May 2024; solid effort over 1m at Bellewstown in April and backed that up with a close third over 6f at Naas; a long way below his best at Leopardstown on latest.
7f maiden winner at Limerick last season on his sixth and final start for Aidan O'Brien; went close in a 6f handicap at Navan four three starts ago; more recent form is much less encouraging.
Two AW wins last year; opened his turf account at the 15th attempt at Naas last week; one of three for the stable here; could feature with the champion jockey booked; draw should help.

OwnerName: B White & M W White & D Sheridan & Ms H McGuinness
Spotlight: Good second at Leopardstown on seasonal debut; race may have come too soon at the Curragh four days later; solid third at Cork next time; hard task now having been raised 9lb for beating Send Harry at Leopardstown; unplaced in this race last year.
Gained second win of career over 1m at Leopardstown on seasonal return last month, beating Zaraahmando by a neck; went up 8lb for that, and Zaraahmando turned the tables last time.

Both wins have come over 1m at Killarney; won a maiden there last summer (yielding to soft) and returned there a year later to record a first handicap success (good); finished 1 3/4l behind Zaraahmando when fourth at Gowran last Saturday.

Prolific winner, latest in Gowran claimer nearly a year ago; 0-10 for current yard; best form this season represented by Down Royal second in May and third at Fairyhouse early this month, both over this trip.

RaceName: Christian Holland/Ken Howell Sports Betting Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 11th of 14 on debut at Lingfield (7f, AW) in November but spectacularly outran odds of 125-1 when third of 12 in a novice at Kempton (1m3f, AW) three weeks ago, nearly taking second; switches to turf but she's in the same ballpark on ratings as the best two of these.

RaceName: Christian Holland/Ken Howell Sports Betting Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Set the pace when last of four at Doncaster (1m2f, good to firm) and ran on from the rear when fourth of ten in a maiden at Pontefract (1m2f, good; 40-1) 17 days later; the latter showed promise but further improvement is needed against all three of today's rivals.

RaceName: Christian Holland/Ken Howell Sports Betting Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: 400,000gns yearling; second in a three-runner novice at Nottingham (1m2f, good) in June, behind a long odds-on favourite, and set the pace when fourth of six in a maiden at Yarmouth (1m2f, good to firm) 18 days later; hooded for both; that's fair form, among the best in this field, and pedigree gives her a good chance to stay 1m4f.

RaceName: Christian Holland/Ken Howell Sports Betting Maiden Fillies' Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
Spotlight: Hood both starts; second of eight at Yarmouth (1m, good to firm) and second of three at Chester (1m2f, good) in another maiden; not bred for this far but the same was true last time when she again did her best work at the finish.
Debut was over 1m4f; down the field in 7f Fairyhouse race in which Sindagan was second.
First foal; dam 5f AW winner, out of a half-sister to a 1m2f Listed winner and to the dam of Cheltenham Gold Cup winner Gaelic Warrior; 4yo Buratino gelding makes belated debut.
Sixth foal; half-brother by Alkumait to two Italian winners and a winning hurdler; dam 1m AW winner, half-sister to an Italian Group-placed winner.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
Spotlight: Showed promise in making the frame in two starts last autumn; placed in three 7f maidens this term; beaten favourite when second at Naas on seasonal debut; eased up late for third at Gowran; rated 83 before chasing home the long odds-on Bamako Beach at Fairyhouse; 13lb rise to 96 may flatter him; obvious chance all the same.
66-1, looked very raw at the Curragh, when finishing in rear in the race in which Starborn Legend was second.

E29,000 Y, E330,000 Breeze Up purchase; had a run in a barrier trial but still looked a bit raw when sixth in an 18-runner contest at the Curragh in early June; confirmed promise when a clear second behind an 82-rated rival in a 6f maiden on second start.
Respectable first outing when fourth in a 1m Gowran maiden won by a stablemate of Sindagan; form of that race has been well-advertised by runner-up Loughrea.
Beaten in excess of 15l in maidens at Limerick and Killarney; up against it.

OwnerName: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
Spotlight: Fair fourth over 1m at Leopardstown on the second of two starts at two; appeared not to see out the extended 1m1f at Gowran on return; better when going close over an extended 7f at Roscommon; should be able to win an average maiden; tough task here against Sindagan, a high-rated gelding in the same colours.
Elzaam filly is the first foal out of a mare who was unplaced over a range of distances; no appeal.

Promising start in 7f maiden at Leopardstown in May, fourth of nine despite racing a shade keenly; again keen and got outpaced over the same trip at the Curragh ten days ago; unlikely to be good enough.

Showed promise in 7f maidens at the Curragh and Gowran on her first two starts; faced a tough task in the Goffs Million; strong form when a short head second to subsequent Sandringham winner Green Carrera in a 1m handicap at the Curragh on seasonal debut; a long way below that form over 1m1f at the same venue last time.
Has finished in front of only two of her 29 rivals in three outings at Dundalk; can be ruled out.
Third foal; Arizona filly, dam of little account but half-sister to two winning hurdlers.
E50,000 yearling (bought in for E75,000 at a Breeze Up last year); sixth foal; half-sister to winners, best of them Asad Zabeel (five races and Listed-placed); dam French middle-distance winner.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Strong in the market on comeback from almost a year off early in the month, when the race didn't set up ideally, and duly won a 1m6f amateurs' handicap on Wolverhampton Tapeta last Tuesday; fair claims under a 5lb penalty.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Hold-up performer who's odds-on to blow the start; landed a hat-trick last summer over about this trip on good to firm ground, latterly off a 1lb higher mark, but not as consistent this time round; needs more.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Went close in a bumper on her debut last spring before not taking to hurdles; well held in three Flat runs this season but this task is more realistic now handicapping and she's one to track in the market.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: His 0-50 classified win here last month has been well advertised since and he just did enough back into a handicap at Leicester (1m4f) last time, despite hanging left on good to firm ground; up 3lb with good chance of the hat-trick.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Has done a lot of his racing at 1m and has often pulled hard when going further, including in the hood (back on tonight; tongue-tie comes off) but does stay this far; not much room for manoeuvre off this mark and needs to leave two lesser efforts behind.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Four defeats at short prices off this sort of mark since two Windsor wins late last summer; didn't look to love the Epsom experience last time, though, and will rightly be popular again; shortlisted.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
OwnerName: Mike Harris Racing & Nikki Evans Racing
Spotlight: Held a couple of times round his beloved Bath in 0-55 company since winning from Bobby Dassler there in the spring; usually dropped in and will want a decent test round this easier course.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Goes well here and took advantage of the drop to 0-50 classified company when winning a weak race over C&D early last month; ran at least as well back into handicap company here four weeks ago to confirm himself still in good form.

RaceName: Alan Bennett Racing/Keith Davies Handicap (Bath Summer Stayers' Series Qualifier)
Spotlight: Irish trainer 14-51 with Flat runners brought over, which entitles this 4yo to some respect; it's hard to find any other positives, though, with him yet to get involved in a finish under either code; the market will likely tell a tale.

Five wins for Johnny Murtagh; went close for this yard at the Curragh in April (7f, soft); below best in four starts since and drawn wide here but drops in grade and is chucked in on last year's best form if rediscovering his best.
French winner has yet to fire since joining this yard; mark is tumbling, however, and he's worth monitoring in the market now dropped in class with cheekpieces back on.
Won over C&D at this meeting in 2024 off 15lb higher; that win came on yielding and his last win came on heavy so while well handicapped, could probably do with a drop of rain.

Gained first turf win off 8lb lower at Limerick (1m, yielding) in June; narrowly denied in follow up bid two days later at Gowran (9.5f, yielding); handles good ground and top rider booked but the draw gods haven't been kind.

Two-time C&D winner on heavy off higher marks; went close again over C&D in October, again on heavy; caught the eye when short of room and not beaten far at Killarney on latest (1m, good); softer conditions would be preferable but he's got plenty of decent form on this sort of ground and his yard targets this meeting; chance.

1m2f winner for Tom Clover last year; best effort for this stable came at Dundalk in March; remote fourth on return from break at Tramore latest (1m4f, good); sharper for that but not sure this shorter trip will suit.

One of two for yard; AW and turf winner for James Ferguson; off the mark for this stable on latest at Bellewstown (1m, good); 8lb rise makes things tougher but this prominent racer is well drawn and can't be discounted for last year's winning yard.
2-5 on the AW; won on turf at Gowran last season (1m, good) off 12lb lower; moderate efforts over further the last twice and may be in handicapper's grip for now.

One of three for yard; 2-16 on turf; won over 1m at Leopardstown (good) last season off 66; scored at Down Royal (7f, good) off 67 in May and just 1lb higher here but in poor form since and needs to revive in new headgear combination.

One of two for yard; back-to-back wins at Leopardstown last summer over 7f on soft and good ground; yet to hit top form this term but is now 2lb below her last win and rider takes off another 3lb; ran poorly at this meeting last year.

OwnerName: Charles Kerwin & Brendan Kerwin & Liam Kehoe
Spotlight: One of three for yard; gained second turf win at Roscommon in May (7.5f, good) off 9lb lower; soundly beaten in three runs since including off lower AW mark latest; drawn wide.

Five-time winner including twice this season; stayed on well to see off Elusive Duke at Ballinrobe (9.5f, gd-yld) eight days ago (Loingseoir fourth) and raised 7lb; has gone well here before but very wide draw not ideal.

OwnerName: W Keeling & M C Grassick & Mrs M J Grassick
Spotlight: Seven-time winner; hold up sort has run respectably in three of his last four starts; stayed on well for fourth behind Lady Arwen at Ballinrobe latest; placed at this meeting over 7f in 2022; ground versatile and could go well granted luck in running.
Five-time winner including here over 7f on heavy; off since a poor run here last October; is 9lb below last win but best form is on testing ground so could do with some rain.

Four-time winner; scored on seasonal return at Cork off 8lb lower; chased home Bay Of Dreams off 2lb lower at Bellewstown on penultimate; never landed a blow behind Lady Arwen at Ballinrobe on latest; visor replaces cheekpieces.
Won a Goodwood novice for James Horton; gradually finding form for this yard and not beaten far at the Curragh on latest; cheekpieces now go on but she's drawn in the car park here.
Decent strike rate on the AW (4-10) but just 1-16 on turf; that win came over 1m2f (good) at Fairyhouse in May; struggled off revised mark twice since and wide draw to overcome here.
One of three for yard; gained second turf win at Gowran in June (1m, yielding), making all; beaten off revised mark twice since and wide draw not ideal for this front runner.

Winner over this trip but doesn't run over it often now, all starts this year having come over 5f; continues to tumble down the weights but has struggled in two runs back on turf latterly and others make more appeal.
No problem with 7f and found the drop to 5f against him last month, when again running well off this mark; stable among the winners and he's high on the shortlist back up in trip.
Closed out last year with a Tapeta win in first-time cheekpieces off 2lb higher; struggled this time round and will need to improve somewhat on previous turf efforts.
Best efforts have all come on Tapeta and he's struggled in both runs this season, having regressed last year; not easy to make a case for him.

Three wins and three seconds from eight runs here and he will be happier sprinting again having not seen out 1m last month; time has looked to be catching up this year, however, and Legendsoftheland appears his trainer's best chance.

Wins have all come after a recent outing and he's having just a second ever run on turf, in a first-time tongue-tie; it's therefore hard to say that everything looks in place for a big run, for a yard also responsible for Honour Your Dreams.

Wins for two previous yards came in the autumn, mainly on the AW, and he's regressed in recent times; the step back up from 5f is a plus off a career-low mark, though, for a trainer who holds more obvious claims with Symbol Of Hope.
Longstanding maiden who's overall continued to regress this year, mainly over 7f; has been offering a bit more again of late, without having the breaks, but others look stronger.

Two years since he last won and five years since he won away from his beloved Bath; one of his better efforts there last time but he is no certainty to reproduce it back up in trip (can pull hard these days).

New trainer won with six of his last 12 runners and is 4-12 with runners here; that's where the positives end, as she showed little for two previous yards (6f-1m) before being picked up for 900gns early last month; watch the market.
